title: Engineering research for ordinary same-day coding tasks

alternate_official_sources.title: Context Engineering for AI Agents: Memory vs. Compaction vs. Tool Clearing
Programmatic Tool Calling with the Claude API
Claude Agent SDK for Python README
Lightweight connection handling for MCP servers

claims.verified_source_fact: A05 §“API Coverage vs. Workflow Tools” says the useful balance depends on the client. §“Context Management” calls for focused results. A08 §“Pagination” requires respecting limits.
claims.inference_or_proposal: Bound the entire source selection and provide a focused ordinary-task path. Preserve the existing full integration for clients that need it.
claims.limits_and_rejection: “Two tools are always better” is unsupported. A smaller schema can still add net overhead. Reject if native task time/usage rises without a compensating measured benefit.

claims.verified_source_fact: A07 §“Prompting for less eagerness” recommends deduplicated paths, stopping when action is possible and tracing only symbols/contracts needed. Its Cursor section describes repeated search caused by overbroad thoroughness instructions.
claims.inference_or_proposal: Replace forced discovery with deterministic hints and narrowly selected primary/direct-helper evidence; remove instructions that require needless lookup on every task.
claims.limits_and_rejection: This is GPT-5 guidance, not an experiment on the pinned Codex model. Do not copy its illustrative “even if ... not fully correct” shortcut or reduce the grader's correctness standard.

claims.verified_source_fact: A01 cell 6 distinguishes whole-transcript compaction, tool-result clearing and external persistent memory. Cells 17–24 describe extra summarizer inference and lost detail.
claims.inference_or_proposal: Ordinary short tasks should not automatically invoke an auxiliary summarizer, extractor or reranker model. A local router can have exactly zero LLM calls by construction.
claims.limits_and_rejection: Zero classifier calls does not mean zero overhead: reading, hashing, formatting, importing and launching the wrapper still count. It also does not prove the routing decision is right.

claims.verified_source_fact: A01 cells 25–32 say clearing drops re-fetchable outputs, can cause repeated reads and invalidates cached prefixes.
claims.inference_or_proposal: Prevent unnecessary content from entering context instead of trying to clear native Codex's internal transcript afterward.
claims.limits_and_rejection: Memglide cannot assume Claude's context-editing API exists in native Codex. Do not invent an equivalent Codex flag or promise history reduction.

claims.verified_source_fact: A01 cells 33–43 show client-side memory storage and a fresh follow-up session with/without saved notes. The analysis explicitly identifies per-read/write tool overhead and dependence on note quality.
claims.inference_or_proposal: Keep explicit, bounded, source-linked decisions/history separate from current source. Warm same-day reuse should validate relevant source versions and count memory creation/maintenance costs.
claims.limits_and_rejection: The notebook comparison is research synthesis, not coding. Plain Markdown notes are a necessary future control; storage alone is not evidence of a Memglide advantage. Do not seed fresh evaluation answers.

claims.verified_source_fact: A04 cells 1–2 and 7 describe matching prompt prefixes, identical tool order, static-first variable-last layout and actual cached-token reporting.
claims.inference_or_proposal: Stabilize the native prompt/schema where controllable; collect total input, cached input and output separately; derive uncached input as input minus cached.
claims.limits_and_rejection: Cached input is a subset of OpenAI total input. Do not add it twice or transfer Anthropic cache accounting. Old-model cache thresholds/discounts/examples do not establish present ChatGPT-authenticated Codex pricing or hit rates. Actual unavailable cost stays null.

claims.verified_source_fact: A02 cells 14–18 keep large raw results in code execution and pass the selected result back to the model. Cell 21 explicitly notes that programmatic invocation can require **more** API calls in the example.
claims.inference_or_proposal: Perform cheap deterministic selection/deduplication before the first native request. An upfront bundle is a simpler candidate than adding another model-authored orchestration stage.
claims.limits_and_rejection: Filtering can shrink content without lowering interactions or latency. No cookbook speed/token percentage is a Memglide result. Actual model-call counts remain unavailable if native telemetry does not expose them.

claims.verified_source_fact: A03 cells 9, 15–16 demonstrate Claude-specific `defer_loading`/`tool_reference` to avoid changing the initial tool prefix.
claims.inference_or_proposal: Avoid adding a broad catalog or dynamic discovery tool to the common short-task path. Omit unused MCP startup/schema exposure in the experimental upfront integration.
claims.limits_and_rejection: These fields are provider features, not native Codex settings. With only two tools, another discovery stage may cost more than it removes.

claims.verified_source_fact: A06 §“Hooks” distinguishes application-invoked deterministic processing from model-invoked tools; §“Custom Tools” describes in-process MCP.
claims.inference_or_proposal: A pre-model local function does not intrinsically require a model call or separate MCP subprocess. Test absence of model/network calls and child processes during routing.
claims.limits_and_rejection: Claude SDK in-process MCP is not proof that native Codex supports the same embedding API. Use a supported native launcher rather than claiming an unimplemented Codex hook.

claims.verified_source_fact: A09 §“Purpose of Evaluations” evaluates useful outcomes, not endpoint coverage. Its questions are stable and verified. A10 preserves per-task duration/tool metrics.
claims.inference_or_proposal: Use fresh ordinary tasks, independent behavioral/regression checks, multiple runs where practical, exact source/prompt settings and per-attempt evidence. Count failures in the assigned cohort.
claims.limits_and_rejection: The MCP guide's exact-string read-only answers, mandated many-call questions and evaluator prompt are unsuitable for code editing. Do not require many calls just to make retrieval look useful. Do not use agent self-reported success as grading.

claims.verified_source_fact: A10 `agent_loop` selects only the first returned tool-use block; A11 forwards only `result.content`. Their example is not a comprehensive native Codex telemetry collector.
claims.inference_or_proposal: Retain Memglide's native structured-output harness, complete MCP event parsing and independent grading rather than importing this evaluator unchanged.
claims.limits_and_rejection: Do not infer all model calls, filesystem reads, structured-result delivery or billing from this example. Missing telemetry is null, with observable proxies labeled as such.

claims.verified_source_fact: A01's illustrative `MemoryToolHandler._resolve` uses a string-prefix containment test; its security note asks for production size limits. A08 warns that annotations are hints, not authorization.
claims.inference_or_proposal: Keep existing component-aware path containment, no-symlink reads, project isolation, byte caps and mutation checks. Test sibling-prefix paths and same-size edits with restored timestamps.
claims.limits_and_rejection: A cookbook is explanatory code, not a security dependency. Source versions do not prove old decisions remain semantically correct after changed requirements.
